verdict.rationale: Keycloak is self-hosted. Its docs cover running it from a container or via the Kubernetes Operator, switching to a production database such as PostgreSQL, and federating users from existing LDAP/AD or custom stores, so the operator decides where identity data lives. There is no documented region or residency selector; residency follows from where the operator deploys Keycloak and its database. Missing for 10: an explicit data-residency or region configuration feature, residency-specific documentation, and independent corroboration of residency control.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Switch to a production ready database such as PostgreSQL.
Run Keycloak from a container image.
Keycloak has built-in support to connect to existing LDAP or Active Directory servers. You can also implement your own provider if you have users in other stores, such as a relational database.
not a bad choice as a self-hosted IAM solution
